messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated OOM rate on runtime pool us-west-gpu-1 (model:redwood-rev1-large). Error spike detected. Alert id=3924681350
ivy_oncall: I'm on it. Any reported customer impact yet?
ben_ml: API error rate ~2.5% for /v1/generate started ~3924681200, visible 14:05Z. Collecting quick telemetry.
sasha_reliability: quick question: kv-cache growth or allocator fragmentation? last similar was alloc churn.
immediate-actions-bot: Took actions: notified CS, started log collector, applied canary changes: batch_size 32->16 on canary nodes, set eviction=aggressive for canary.
miriam_support: CS notes: 3 paying orgs reported truncated outputs/retries. CS outreach started.
ben_ml: paste telemetry snippet for canary node:
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-17T14:05:10Z
nvidia-smi:
GPU0 total=24576 MiB used=24102 MiB
Processes: python(1234) 14.7G, python(2345) 9.3G
KV-cache ~= 18.5 GiB
batch_size configured 32 -> canary 16
OOMs observed: 12 in last 10m
```
telemetry-bot: KV-cache metrics: prefix hit rate +22% last 30m, eviction_rate down 60% (eviction thread lag). Possibility: pinned entries not reclaimed.
sasha_reliability: hypotheses: H1) fragmentation due to many small frees + large contiguous alloc requests. H2) workload spike increased batch tokens leading to KV balloon. H3) eviction bug leaving large pinned entries.
ivy_oncall: Actions executed: canary batch->16, eviction aggressive, rolling restart of affected subset. Can a small experiment reduce max_batch_tokens to 1024 on a non-prod pool? Might show correlation.
ben_ml: starting experiment on pool dev-try: max_batch_tokens 2048->1024. Monitoring memory and OOM count.
telemetry-bot: experiment queued id=exp-3924681350-1
log-collector: logs and heap snapshots uploading: https://internal-logs.redwood/team/3924681350/kvcache_dump.tar.gz
sasha_reliability: allocator grep shows repeated "failed_alloc size=34816000 alignment=256" entries; free lists contain many small blocks. Points to fragmentation. Trace saved: s3://redwood-incidents/3924681350/alloc_trace.txt
ben_ml: experiment results (10m): dev-try mem usage down ~28%, OOMs -> 0 in window. Strong signal batch token cap helps.
immediate-actions-bot: Canary metrics: error rate dropped from 2.5% -> 0.4% within ~6m after canary changes and restart.
miriam_support: CX impact timeline posted: https://confluence.redwood/ops/incidents/3924681350-impact. Affected window ~14:02Z-14:36Z for some customers.
ivy_oncall: Next mitigations: continue rolling restarts until pool stable, backport allocator defrag patch (PR #4382) to staging, implement per-request KV size cap. Can someone run an evict-thread health check and increase its scheduling priority?
sasha_reliability: I'll open PR to bump eviction thread niceness and add eviction lag alert. Adding to RCA hypotheses: H4) eviction thread scheduling caused backlog.
ben_ml: I've uploaded flamegraphs + allocator timeline to the RCA folder. archive: s3://redwood-incidents/3924681350/archive.tar.gz
log-collector: collection complete.
immediate-actions-bot: commands executed (for audit):
```
redwood ctl pool update us-west-gpu-1 --selector canary --set batch_size=16
redwood ctl runtime set-eviction --pool us-west-gpu-1 --mode aggressive
redwood ctl pool update dev-try --set max_batch_tokens=1024
redwood ctl node restart --pool us-west-gpu-1 --selector canary
```
ivy_oncall: Assigning postmortem owners: lead=ivy_oncall, alloc analysis=ben_ml, runtime fixes=sasha_reliability, customer comms=miriam_support. ETA initial RCA draft: 72h.
ben_ml: adding note: consider allocator defrag on warmup and limit for KV per-request cap.
sasha_reliability: logging in-thread checklist for RCA: [collect alloc traces], [compare before/after batch token experiment], [eviction thread profiling], [verify per-request kv limits], [customer impact summary].
immediate-actions-bot: Incident mitigation state: mitigated. Reopen if error rate >1% or OOMs resume.
ivy_oncall: thanks team. I'll start the RCA doc and link collected artifacts. Closing live coordination thread.
ben_ml: :thumbsup: will follow up with detailed analysis and recommended rollout plan for allocator patch.
